Only with `--dry-run`.

A stored hazard memory says that in staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket. A real run against staging could therefore write to prod. The memory says never to run `scripts/export.py` against staging without `--dry-run`.

The script supports that flag. In its current form it only prints `exporting staging to <bucket> (dry_run=True)` and doesn't write anything, so a dry run is safe. It also lets you confirm which bucket staging resolves to:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

If the printed bucket is the prod one, the memory is still accurate.

Two caveats:
- The script doesn't actually use `--dry-run` to gate anything yet, because it has no export logic. When real export code gets added, make sure it honors the flag before anyone relies on this.
- I haven't run the command myself, since it depends on your staging environment variables. Say so if you want me to run it.

For a real (non-dry) staging test, point `EXPORT_BUCKET` at a dedicated test bucket first, for example `EXPORT_BUCKET=ledgerline-exports-staging-test`. That bucket name is only an example, so I'd confirm it exists and is separate from prod before using it.
